environment.postgres_lifecycle: mission services.yaml start, healthcheck, and stop commands only
environment.network: not required; analyzer isolation records that plain subprocesses do not prove network denial

measurement_order: record the plan commit without changing budgets or tolerances
start and healthcheck PostgreSQL through services.yaml

cases.comparison_method: Compare incremental SHA-256 and byte count with an independent whole-file SHA-256.
cases.acceptance_rule: All samples use 65536-byte bounded reads, preserve byte count, match the independent digest, and remain within both resource budgets.
limitations: The committed 2 MiB synthetic fixture is a bounded proof, not a 1 GiB release-load result.

cases.comparison_method: Write each source byte sequence to a new file and compare the exact readback bytes and aggregate SHA-256.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every one of at least six byte classes round-trips exactly in every sample within both resource budgets.
limitations: This prototype tests filesystem custody, not HTTP transfer framing.

cases.comparison_method: Instrument compression output before AES-GCM, decrypt then decompress, compare source digest, and mutate the authentication tag.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every sample proves compression precedes AEAD, exact readback succeeds, a one-bit ciphertext mutation fails, and both resource budgets hold.
limitations: The disposable deterministic nonce is safe only for this one-shot prototype and must not be copied into production.

cases.comparison_method: Create disposable PostgreSQL 17 partitions, insert bytea-only synthetic ciphertext, compare row/partition counts and inspect pruning and schema columns.
cases.acceptance_rule: All samples observe PostgreSQL 17 on port 5440, 200 rows, two partitions, no content plaintext column, pruning evidence, and both resource budgets.
limitations: The row count is a research proof, not production sizing guidance.

cases.comparison_method: Compare HMAC-SHA-256 equality tokens within and across organization, field, and generation scope.
cases.acceptance_rule: Same-scope equality matches; organization, field, and generation changes produce different fixed-length tokens within both resource budgets.
limitations: Equality and frequency leakage within a scope remains and is explicitly recorded.

inputs: old and new synthetic wrapping roots
cases.comparison_method: Wrap one DEK under two AES-GCM roots and compare wrapped material, payload ciphertext digest, source digest, and checkpoint.
cases.acceptance_rule: Wrapped material changes while payload ciphertext and source identity remain unchanged, and every sample stays within both resource budgets.
limitations: No cloud KMS call is made; provider conformance remains later work.

inputs: one injected rollback after decision and audit writes
cases.comparison_method: Use one PostgreSQL transaction for committed state and roll back the injected fault before receipt creation, then compare table counts.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every sample has exactly one committed decision, audit, and receipt, no faulted row, PostgreSQL 17 on 5440, and both resource budgets.
limitations: Process-death and fsync fault injection remain production-stage durability tests.

cases.comparison_method: Inspect child-visible environment, directory, descriptor limit, output size, and timeout while explicitly testing whether network denial is proven.
cases.acceptance_rule: Resource and ambient-state bounds hold, but acceptance requires the honest conclusion that a plain subprocess does not prove network denial.
limitations: This negative result rejects plain subprocess isolation as the complete hostile-extension boundary.

inputs: one late event and superseding replay
cases.comparison_method: Digest ordered immutable snapshots in PostgreSQL, repeat the pinned snapshot, add a late event, and append a superseding run.
cases.acceptance_rule: Recorded replay digests match, late replay differs, all three runs remain, PostgreSQL 17 on 5440, and both resource budgets hold.
limitations: Tenant fairness and crash recovery need larger production-stage fault tests.
